title: Process, worn, reveal
hook: This Dior bow hadn't been worn in decades.
why: A short arc of a process shot, the piece worn, then the reveal fits 15–30 seconds and keeps people watching to the end.
adapt: Polish one piece on the wooden tray, clip it on, finish on a close-up in window light, the same light as our product photos.

title: Pack an order with me
hook: Packing a vintage Chanel order for London.
why: Jewellery brands use 'pack an order with me' clips: they show the care that goes into each order and what arrives at the door.
adapt: Tissue, ribbon, the KARINEKO card, the box closing. Quiet sound of paper. No customer names or addresses on screen.

title: Three ways to wear one piece
hook: One vintage Chanel brooch, three ways.
why: Styling and close-up content sells: seeing a piece worn up close makes people want it.
adapt: One brooch: on a lapel, on a ribbon as a necklace, on a bag strap. Hands and outfits only, real photos.

title: How to tell a real vintage logo
hook: Three things we check on every vintage Dior piece.
why: Short educational clips build trust, and vintage sellers use them alongside style guides and footage of the team at work.
adapt: Turn our guide on dating vintage Chanel jewellery into 30 seconds: the stamp, the clasp, the weight. Link the guide in bio.

title: The rare piece reveal
hook: The rarest piece we've had this year.
why: Creative reveals that go beyond a plain unboxing drive reach and comments.
adapt: Slow reveal of the week's standout piece from under linen, a turn in the light, the price at the end.

title: Get ready with me, jewellery last
hook: Getting ready for dinner in London. The last step is the hardest.
why: GRWM is still the anchor beauty format on TikTok: entertainment, a little education and product shown in use, all in one.
adapt: A real GRWM filmed on our own phone; the final step is choosing between two Dior pieces. No AI images of people.

title: Jewellery loading bar
why: The Makeup Loading Bar format builds a look step by step with an on-screen progress bar, so people stay to see 100%.
adapt: Earrings 25%, necklace 50%, ring 75%, brooch 100%. Each step a close-up.

title: Which would you wear?
hook: Gold or silver for this Dior bow?
why: Threads rewards conversation and personality over polish; over-produced posts tend to do worse there.
adapt: Two photos of the same design in gold and silver. Ask which one, and reply to every answer.

title: What we check before buying a piece
hook: Before a piece reaches the shop, we check four things.
why: Behind-the-scenes posts are a staple of Threads idea lists, and a few thoughtful posts a week beat one polished post a month.
adapt: A short thread: the stamp, the clasp, the plating, the weight. One photo per point.

title: Customer spotlight, with permission
why: Client spotlights shared with permission are on every Threads idea list; real customers make the shop feel trustworthy.
adapt: Ask a customer for a photo of them wearing their piece, and caption it in their own words. Always ask first.
